pages.text: The disbelievers of Quraysh drove the Prophet ﷺ out of his town, Makkah, and he set out with his companion Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him).
The two of them took refuge in a cave in the mountain of Thawr in Makkah, and they stayed there for three nights.
Abu Bakr was afraid for the Prophet ﷺ, and while the two of them were in the cave he said: “If one of them were to look down beneath his feet, he would see us.” (Sahih al-Bukhari 3653)
The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two, the third of whom is Allah?” (Sahih al-Bukhari 3653)

Allah mentioned this in the Qur'an: ﴿إِذۡ هُمَا فِي ٱلۡغَارِ إِذۡ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحۡزَنۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَاۖ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'when the two of them were in the cave, when he said to his companion: Do not grieve; Allah is with us. Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon him' — that is, He sent down calm into the heart of His Messenger ﷺ, and saved him from his enemy.

In this story, Allah was with His Prophet and his companion with His help and support; and in it is a great honour for Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), the companion of the Prophet ﷺ in the cave.
